```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
here::i_am("errata.qmd")

out <- function(f) read_csv(here("maintained", "output", f), show_col_types = FALSE)

distances <- out("appendix_table_1_distance_tests.csv")
counts <- out("appendix_table_1_distance_counts.csv")
# What the deposit's own procedure does over 200 seeds, which is entry 7's evidence that
# the published columns are not reproducible.
headline <- out("appendix_table_1_bootstrap_headline.csv")
demos <- out("table_1_demographics.csv")
fig1 <- out("figure_1_standardized_demos.csv")
welfare_ns <- out("table_4_welfare_ns.csv")
kamsimas <- out("table_6_kamsimas.csv")
hiscox <- out("table_7_hiscox.csv")

# The string the article prints, kept as a string: a type guess turns 0.100 into 0.1 and
# destroys the precision the page carries.
published <- read_csv(here("ground_truth", "published_claims.csv"),
                      col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))

# Every number in a corrected sentence below is computed here, at the time this document
# is rendered, from the deposited data. That includes the numbers that were not wrong: a
# token carried over from the published sentence is inherited on trust, and rendering the
# whole sentence from the pipeline is what verifies it.
cell <- function(tab, var, col) {
  value <- tab[[col]][tab$variable == var]
  stopifnot(length(value) == 1)
  as.numeric(str_remove_all(str_extract(value, "^[$]?-?[0-9,.]+"), "[$,]"))
}

standardized <- function(var, survey_id) {
  value <- fig1$mean[fig1$variable == var & fig1$survey == survey_id]
  stopifnot(length(value) == 1)
  value
}

dist_row <- function(var) {
  row <- distances[distances$variable == var, ]
  stopifnot(nrow(row) == 1)
  row
}

# The article's own cell, quoted rather than retyped.
page <- function(id) {
  value <- published$value_paper[published$claim_id == id]
  stopifnot(length(value) == 1)
  value
}

fitted_n <- function(tab, key, value) {
  n <- unique(tab$nobs[tab[[key]] == value])
  stopifnot(length(n) == 1)
  n
}

# Recomputed from the distance and standard error appendix Table 1 itself prints, so this
# arithmetic does not depend on rerunning the deposit's unseeded bootstrap.
published_a1 <- published |>
  filter(str_starts(claim_id, "a1_")) |>
  transmute(quantity = str_extract(claim_id, "(?<=^a1_)[a-z]+"),
            variable = str_remove(claim_id, "^a1_[a-z]+_"),
            value = as.numeric(value_paper)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = quantity, values_from = value) |>
  mutate(z = distance / se, p_twotail = 2 * pnorm(-abs(z)))

page_z <- function(var) published_a1$z[published_a1$variable == var]
page_p_twotail <- function(var) published_a1$p_twotail[published_a1$variable == var]

trait_vars <- c("extraversion", "agreeableness", "conscientiousness",
                "emotionalstability", "opennesstoexperiences")
trait_rows <- filter(distances, variable %in% trait_vars)
traits_significant <- sum(trait_rows$lucid_is_closer > 0 & trait_rows$p_twotail < 0.05)

demographic_vars <- c("female", "education", "age", "income", "race_white", "race_black",
                      "race_hispanic", "region_northeast", "region_midwest",
                      "region_south", "region_west")
demographic_rows <- filter(distances, variable %in% demographic_vars)
demographic_closer <- sum(demographic_rows$lucid_is_closer > 0)
demographic_significant <- sum(demographic_rows$lucid_is_closer > 0 &
                                 demographic_rows$p_archive < 0.05)
demographic_names <- demographic_rows$varname[demographic_rows$lucid_is_closer > 0 &
                                                demographic_rows$p_archive < 0.05]

# ENTRY 7. The published standard error and p-value columns against this run's, both sides
# rounded to the three decimals appendix Table 1 prints before they are compared, because
# the entry is about what the page shows rather than about the precision behind it.
a1_compare <- published_a1 |>
  select(variable, page_distance = distance, page_se = se, page_p = p) |>
  left_join(select(distances, variable, run_distance = lucid_is_closer,
                   run_se = se, run_p = p_archive), by = "variable") |>
  mutate(across(everything(), identity),
         distance_differs = sprintf("%.3f", page_distance) != sprintf("%.3f", run_distance),
         se_differs = sprintf("%.3f", page_se) != sprintf("%.3f", run_se),
         p_differs = sprintf("%.3f", page_p) != sprintf("%.3f", run_p))
stopifnot(nrow(a1_compare) == nrow(published_a1), !anyNA(a1_compare$run_se))
n_a1_rows <- nrow(a1_compare)
n_a1_distance_differ <- sum(a1_compare$distance_differs)
n_a1_se_differ <- sum(a1_compare$se_differs)
n_a1_p_differ <- sum(a1_compare$p_differs)

# The implied Monte Carlo standard deviation of the largest printed standard error. The
# sampling error of a bootstrap SD is about SE / sqrt(2B), so this is derived from two
# quantities the pipeline already records rather than from a rerun over several seeds,
# which would cost an hour to say the same thing.
a1_mc_sd <- max(distances$se) / sqrt(2 * counts$n_resamples)
a1_mc_share <- 0.001 / a1_mc_sd

# Entry 7 corrects every cell of both columns, so it cites every one of their ground-truth
# rows. Naming the shape rather than an instance is the point: the entry is about the two
# columns, not about any one standard error in them.
a1_claim_ids <- published |>
  filter(str_detect(claim_id, "^a1_(se|p)_")) |>
  pull(claim_id) |>
  sort() |>
  str_c(collapse = ";")

# A corrected count that the article spelled out has to come back as a word.
words <- c("zero", "one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight",
           "nine", "ten", "eleven", "twelve", "thirteen", "fourteen", "fifteen",
           "sixteen", "seventeen", "eighteen", "nineteen", "twenty")
word <- function(n) words[[n + 1]]
num <- function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)

# One decimal on the percentage point scale throughout, and thousands separators on a
# sample size, matching the appendix's own typography.
pts <- function(x) str_replace(sprintf("%.1f", x), "^-", "\u2013")
sd_fmt <- function(x) str_replace(sprintf("%.3f", x), "^-", "\u2013")
n_fmt <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)

# The appendix prints its p-values to three decimals, so a corrected p-value does too.
p_fmt <- function(x) sprintf("%.3f", x)
```

```{r entries}
# THE ERRATA SPINE. Every entry is defined once, here, and rendered from here: into this
# document, and into whatever else needs it, which reads the errata_entries.csv written at
# the bottom of this file rather than keeping a second hand-typed copy.
#
# [[...]] marks the span that changes. Each renderer supplies its own markup for it: bold
# here, \was{} in an edition. Nothing else in a field is markup, so the same string can be
# set by either. NOTHING ELSE MEANS NOTHING ELSE: `published` is the sentence as the page
# sets it and nothing more. Entries 4 and 5 used to end theirs with a bracketed
# "[Online appendix, section 2.1.3]", which is not on the page, is already the `location`
# column's job, and made `published` and `corrected` differ by a clause as well as by the
# marked span. An edition patches by finding `published` in the carried-across text, so a
# field carrying a locator matches nothing and the entry is skipped IN SILENCE; both were,
# and the appendix builder's routing assertion is what said so. A locator a reader needs
# goes in `note`. Every unmarked number in a corrected sentence is computed too, so a reader
# diffing published against corrected sees the whole sentence verified.
#
# Numbering follows PROCEDURES.md Stage 4b: entries are ordered by severity block (quantity;
# description, interpretation, definition; label, float, cross_reference; wording, spelling,
# typography; bibliographic), discovery order inside a block, and a finding that lands in an
# earlier block renumbers the entries after it. Renumbered 2026-11-07; the old-to-new map is
# in that day's commit message.
#
# claim_ids names the ground-truth rows an entry corrects, semicolon-separated, so that "is
# this finding published?" is a query rather than a judgment. Entries 1 and 2 each carry the
# method row appendix_two_tailed_method alongside their own claim, because that row is the
# cause both descend from and it is stated in the preamble rather than in an entry of its
# own. Entry 2's own number matches the deposit, which is the point: the article agrees with
# its own code and both depart from the test the appendix describes. Every id listed here is
# checked against the ground truth by build_ground_truth.R.
#
# corrected_values runs parallel to claim_ids, one value per id in the same order, carrying
# the corrected quantity as a number rather than as a sentence, on the claim's scale. Each
# value comes from the same expression that glues the sentence, so the two cannot be written
# apart, and the gate below re-checks that each one is still inside the span it belongs to.
# An entry of a class that changes no quantity, and a note, carries NA.
values_unresolved <- integer(0)
entries <- tribble(
  ~entry, ~class, ~source, ~form, ~title, ~location, ~published, ~corrected, ~note, ~claim_ids, ~corrected_values,

  1, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "Lucid is not significantly closer than MTurk on all five personality traits",
  "app. Section 1",
  "Formal hypothesis tests demonstrate that Lucid is significantly closer to the ANES 2012 than MTurk on [[all five traits]].",
  str_glue("Formal hypothesis tests demonstrate that Lucid is significantly closer to the ANES 2012 than MTurk on [[{word(traits_significant)} of the five traits, extraversion excepted]]."),
  str_glue(
    "Appendix Table 1 prints {page('a1_distance_extraversion')} and ",
    "{page('a1_se_extraversion')} for extraversion's distance and bootstrapped standard ",
    "error. Those two numbers give `z` = {sprintf('%.2f', page_z('extraversion'))} and a ",
    "two-tailed p-value of {p_fmt(page_p_twotail('extraversion'))}, above the 0.05 ",
    "threshold; the table's own p-value column prints {page('a1_p_extraversion')}, which is ",
    "the deposit's expression rather than the two-tailed test. The maintained rewrite's ",
    "seeded run reaches the same conclusion, at `z` = ",
    "{sprintf('%.2f', dist_row('extraversion')$z)} and p = ",
    "{p_fmt(dist_row('extraversion')$p_twotail)}. The other four traits clear 0.05 by a ",
    "wide margin under either test."),
  "traits_all_five_significantly_closer;appendix_two_tailed_method",
  str_c(as.integer(traits_significant == 5), ";NA"),

  2, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "The number of significant differences in the online appendix",
  "app. Section 1",
  "Out of 21 opportunities, Lucid is closer to the ANES 18 times, [[14]] of which are significant.",
  str_glue("Out of {counts$n_variables} opportunities, Lucid is closer to the ANES {counts$n_lucid_closer} times, [[{counts$n_sig_closer_twotail}]] of which are significant."),
  str_glue(
    "Extraversion is the difference between the two counts, for the reason given above. ",
    "Recomputing every p-value from the distance and standard error appendix Table 1 prints ",
    "gives the same {counts$n_sig_closer_twotail}. The sentence that follows it is ",
    "unaffected: MTurk is closer in {counts$n_mturk_closer} instances and significant in ",
    "{word(counts$n_sig_farther_twotail)}, voter turnout, under both tests."),
  "appendix_lucid_closer_significant;appendix_two_tailed_method",
  str_c(counts$n_sig_closer_twotail, ";NA"),

  3, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "Six demographic differences are significant, not five",
  "main text",
  "Out of the 11 demographic variables that are measured for both Lucid and MTurk, the Lucid mean is closer to the ANES mean in nine instances, [[five]] of which are statistically significant.",
  str_glue("Out of the {nrow(demographic_rows)} demographic variables that are measured for both Lucid and MTurk, the Lucid mean is closer to the ANES mean in {word(demographic_closer)} instances, [[{word(demographic_significant)}]] of which are statistically significant."),
  str_glue(
    "Appendix Table 1 prints a p-value below 0.05 for ",
    "{str_c(str_c(head(demographic_names, -1), collapse = ', '), ' and ', tail(demographic_names, 1))}, ",
    "and Lucid is the closer sample on all {word(demographic_significant)}. The count is the ",
    "same under the two-tailed test corrected in the first two entries, so it does not turn ",
    "on which p-value is used."),
  "demographic_significantly_closer",
  num(demographic_significant),

  4, "quantity", "pipeline", "brief",
  "The sample size of the Lucid welfare replication",
  "app. Section 2.1.3",
  "Sample: [[1,811]] Lucid respondents.",
  str_glue("Sample: [[{n_fmt(welfare_ns$n[welfare_ns$survey == 'lucid'])}]] Lucid respondents."),
  str_glue(
    "The sentence is in section 2.1.3 of the online appendix. ",
    "{n_fmt(fitted_n(hiscox, 'survey', 'lucid'))} is the Lucid sample of the Hiscox ",
    "free-trade replication, reported in section 2.4.2 of the same appendix. The welfare ",
    "data hold {n_fmt(welfare_ns$rows[welfare_ns$survey == 'lucid'])} Lucid rows, of which ",
    "{n_fmt(welfare_ns$n[welfare_ns$survey == 'lucid'])} have a usable outcome, and the ",
    "manifest reports the analysed sample in every other section."),
  "manifest_welfare_lucid_n",
  num(welfare_ns$n[welfare_ns$survey == 'lucid']),

  5, "quantity", "pipeline", "brief",
  "The sample size of the original Kam and Simas study",
  "app. Section 2.3.1",
  "Sample: [[761]] respondents gathered from a Knowledge Networks national probability sample.",
  str_glue("Sample: [[{n_fmt(fitted_n(kamsimas, 'model', 'kam_base'))}]] respondents gathered from a Knowledge Networks national probability sample."),
  str_glue(
    "The sentence is in section 2.3.1 of the online appendix. ",
    "Appendix Table 2 reports N = {n_fmt(fitted_n(kamsimas, 'model', 'kam_base'))} for all ",
    "three models fitted to this sample, and {n_fmt(fitted_n(kamsimas, 'model', 'kam_base'))} ",
    "is what the deposited data give. The manifest reports the analysed sample rather than ",
    "the source study's throughout: its entry for the 1984 General Social Survey gives ",
    "{n_fmt(welfare_ns$n[welfare_ns$survey == 'GSS84'])}, where the deposited file holds ",
    "{n_fmt(welfare_ns$rows[welfare_ns$survey == 'GSS84'])} respondents for that survey."),
  "manifest_ks_original_n",
  num(fitted_n(kamsimas, 'model', 'kam_base')),

  6, "description", "pipeline", "full",
  "The MTurk sample under-represents southerners",
  "main text",
  "The regional balance on Lucid comes very close to the 2012 ANES, whereas the MTurk sample appears to [[overrepresent]] southerners.",
  "The regional balance on Lucid comes very close to the 2012 ANES, whereas the MTurk sample appears to [[underrepresent]] southerners.",
  str_glue(
    "The southern share is {pts(cell(demos, 'region_south', 'mturk'))} per cent on MTurk ",
    "against the ANES 2012 benchmark of {pts(cell(demos, 'region_south', 'anes2012'))}, so ",
    "MTurk sits ",
    "{pts(abs(cell(demos, 'region_south', 'mturk') - cell(demos, 'region_south', 'anes2012')))} ",
    "points below it; Lucid is at {pts(cell(demos, 'region_south', 'lucid'))}. Figure 1, ",
    "which is where the sentence sends the reader, plots the same thing in standard ",
    "deviations: MTurk at {sd_fmt(standardized('region_south', 'mturk'))} and Lucid at ",
    "{sd_fmt(standardized('region_south', 'lucid'))}, with the benchmark at zero. MTurk ",
    "over-represents the Northeast and the Midwest instead. Appendix Table 1 is unaffected: ",
    "it reports the distance between the two samples rather than the direction of either, ",
    "and its South row is right."),
  "mturk_overrepresents_southerners",
  NA_character_,

  7, "float", "pipeline", "full",
  "The standard errors and p-values of appendix Table 1 are one draw from an unseeded bootstrap",
  "online app. Table 1",
  str_glue(
    "Table 1's Bootstrapped SE and p-value columns are [[one draw from a ",
    "{n_fmt(100)}-resample bootstrap for which the deposited code sets no seed]]. Neither ",
    "column is reproducible: running the deposited procedure again moves it, and moves the ",
    "count of significant differences the appendix states along with it."),
  str_glue(
    "[[This edition prints a {n_fmt(counts$n_resamples)}-resample bootstrap at a declared ",
    "seed]]. All {n_a1_rows} distances are unchanged and reproduce the published column ",
    "exactly; {word(n_a1_se_differ)} of the {n_a1_rows} standard errors and ",
    "{word(n_a1_p_differ)} of the {n_a1_rows} p-values differ from it at the three decimals ",
    "the table prints."),
  str_glue(
    "The sampling error of a bootstrap standard deviation is about `SE / sqrt(2B)`. At the ",
    "deposit's `B` = {n_fmt(100)} that is roughly 0.0035 on a standard error near 0.05, ",
    "three times the last digit the table prints, which is why ",
    "`appendix_table_1_bootstrap_stability.R` recovers the published count of ",
    "{page('appendix_lucid_closer_significant')} significant differences on only ",
    "{sprintf('%.1f', 100 * headline$share_archive_equals_14)} per cent of 200 seeds, ",
    "ranging {headline$archive_min} to {headline$archive_max}. At ",
    "`B` = {n_fmt(counts$n_resamples)} it falls to {sprintf('%.5f', a1_mc_sd)}, about a ",
    "{word(round(a1_mc_share))}th of that last digit, and the printed column stops being a ",
    "property of the seed. Nothing here moves a distance, a sign, or the size of any ",
    "difference, which is what the appendix's argument rests on. What it does settle is ",
    "the two counts corrected in entries 1 and 2: at this precision they no longer turn on ",
    "which of the two p-value expressions is used, because extraversion falls short of 0.05 ",
    "under both."),
  a1_claim_ids,
  NA_character_,

  # THE FIRST ENTRY THAT IS NOT ABOUT THE DEPOSIT, and the first whose source is the
  # remastered edition rather than this pipeline. It corrects no quantity and cites no
  # ground-truth row, because the defect is a space the appendix page does not set and
  # nothing in the deposited data bears on it. Decision 6 of the remaster protocol is
  # what admits it: no error is too small, or a remastered edition does not mean
  # anything. Found by reading the rendered pages side by side, which is the only pass
  # in this programme that reaches typography at all.
  8, "typography", "reading", "brief",
  "A missing space in the healthcare rumor study manifest",
  "app. Section 2.5.1",
  "[[Control:(No]] introduction before asking the rumor belief question.)",
  "[[Control: (No]] introduction before asking the rumor belief question.)",
  str_glue(
    "The item is in section 2.5.1 of the online appendix. The published page sets no ",
    "space between the bold `Control:` and the parenthesis after it, where the parallel ",
    "item in section 2.4.1 sets one and so does every other labelled condition in the ",
    "manifest. It is the page's own spacing and not an extraction artifact: read off the ",
    "rendered PDF at 300 dpi, the bold run ends and the roman run begins at the same ",
    "horizontal position, against a gap of one space width in section 2.4.1. No ",
    "comparison of text can see it, because a space is not a token."),
  # EMPTY AND NOT NA: write_csv puts the literal string "NA" in the file, and the
  # remaster's Python reader takes the cell as text without a missing-value
  # convention, so the spine would carry a claim id called NA.
  "",
  NA_character_,

  # A DROPPED WORD, SUPPLIED. Decision 13 of the remaster protocol allows it
  # where the replacement is recoverable from the document rather than invented
  # for it, and this one is not quite: the sentence wants a verb after "to" and
  # "imply", "say" and "suggest" all fit. Alex, 2026-09-19, shown the three:
  # go with "imply". It is recorded as a choice in the note rather than passed
  # off as a transcription.
  9, "wording", "reading", "full",
  "A missing word in the Discussion",
  "main text p. 12",
  str_c("While we think the theories that underlie most survey experiments ",
        "conducted in the USA would extend to Lucid, we emphatically do not ",
        "mean [[to]] that any experiment conducted on a convenience sample is ",
        "relevant for theory."),
  str_c("While we think the theories that underlie most survey experiments ",
        "conducted in the USA would extend to Lucid, we emphatically do not ",
        "mean [[to imply]] that any experiment conducted on a convenience ",
        "sample is relevant for theory."),
  str_c("The published page sets \"do not mean to that\", which is ",
        "ungrammatical: a verb is missing after \"to\". The authors' own ",
        "LaTeX source for the article, in the archived working folder, reads ",
        "the same, so the omission is not the publisher's typesetting. The ",
        "paragraph around it separates a theory's predictions extending to a ",
        "sample from that sample being drawn at random from a population, and ",
        "the sentence is the authors declining the stronger reading of their ",
        "own argument, so the missing verb is one of \"imply\", \"say\" or ",
        "\"suggest\". \"Imply\" is the one supplied here and the choice is ",
        "recorded rather than presented as a reading of the page: nothing in ",
        "the paragraph turns on which of the three it is."),
  "",
  NA_character_
) |>
  mutate(across(c(title, published, corrected, note, claim_ids, corrected_values), as.character))

stopifnot(nrow(entries) == max(entries$entry), !anyDuplicated(entries$entry))

# values_in_spans is FALSE where the claim's scale is not the sentence's, under PROCEDURES'
# rule that corrected_values is always on the claim's scale. A method row or other id with
# no number on any scale stores NA in its position. Such an entry's note must say why.
off_claim_scale <- c(1, 2)
entries <- entries |>
  mutate(values_in_spans = case_when(
    is.na(corrected_values) ~ NA,
    entry %in% off_claim_scale ~ FALSE,
    .default = TRUE
  ))
stopifnot(all(str_length(entries$note[!replace_na(entries$values_in_spans, TRUE)]) > 0))

# Gate: corrected_values agrees with the sentence it was glued into ----
# The column and the sentence are written from one expression, so they begin in agreement
# and this gate exists for the edit that separates them: a value moved from one marked span
# to another, a span reworded to carry a second number, a claim id appended without its
# value. Each value has to be inside the span it belongs to, matched by position where the
# counts line up, and inside SOME span where an entry marks a label as well as a number and
# its spans outnumber its values. The spelled form is tolerated ("four" for 4), and so is a
# thousands separator.
marked_spans <- function(x) str_match_all(x, "\\[\\[(.*?)\\]\\]")[[1]][, 2]
gate_words <- c("zero", "one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight", "nine", "ten")
in_span <- function(v, s) {
  s <- str_remove_all(s, ",")
  spelled <- if (str_detect(v, "^[0-9]+$") && as.integer(v) < length(gate_words)) gate_words[as.integer(v) + 1] else v
  str_detect(s, fixed(v)) || str_detect(s, fixed(spelled))
}

quantified <- entries |>
  filter(!is.na(corrected_values), values_in_spans) |>
  mutate(ids = str_split(claim_ids, ";"), values = str_split(corrected_values, ";"),
         spans = map(corrected, marked_spans))

stopifnot(all(lengths(quantified$ids) == lengths(quantified$values)))

value_placed <- pmap_lgl(quantified, function(...) {
  e <- list(...)
  if (length(e$values) == length(e$spans)) {
    all(map2_lgl(e$values, e$spans, in_span))
  } else {
    all(map_lgl(e$values, \(v) any(map_lgl(e$spans, \(s) in_span(v, s)))))
  }
})

if (!all(value_placed)) {
  print(quantified |> filter(!value_placed) |> select(entry, title, corrected_values, corrected))
  stop("An entry's corrected_values are not in the spans of its corrected sentence.")
}

# An entry that changes a quantity has to say which one, and an entry that changes none, or
# a note, may not carry a value. The class is the declaration and this is where it binds.
# Empty claim_ids is stored as "" and counts as missing.
no_claim <- is.na(entries$claim_ids) | entries$claim_ids == ""
stopifnot(
  all(!is.na(entries$corrected_values[entries$class == "quantity" & entries$form != "note" & !no_claim &
                                        !entries$entry %in% values_unresolved])),
  all(is.na(entries$corrected_values[entries$class != "quantity" | entries$form == "note"])),
  all(is.na(entries$corrected_values) | !no_claim)
)


# The spine's markup, resolved for this document. Another renderer resolves it differently.
bold <- function(x) str_replace_all(x, "\\[\\[(.*?)\\]\\]", "**\\1**")

# A heading is only a heading when a blank line precedes it, which is why every emitted
# entry opens with one.
emit <- function(n) {
  e <- entries |> filter(entry == n)
  cat("\n\n## ", e$entry, ". ", e$title, "\n\n> ", bold(e$published),
      "\n\nCorrected:\n\n> ", bold(e$corrected), "\n\n", e$note, "\n", sep = "")
}
```

This note lists `r word(nrow(entries))` corrections to "Validating the demographic, political, psychological, and experimental results obtained from a new source of online survey respondents," published in *Research and Politics* 6(1), doi [10.1177/2053168018822174](https://doi.org/10.1177/2053168018822174). **None of them changes a conclusion of the paper.** Two are counts of statistically significant differences in the online appendix, one reverses the direction of a descriptive comparison, one is a count off by one, two are sample sizes in the appendix study manifest, one is the bootstrap behind appendix Table 1, which the deposited code leaves unseeded and runs too few times to settle the third decimal it prints, one is a missing space in the appendix study manifest, and one supplies a word the Discussion drops. The paper's finding, that Lucid respondents track US national benchmarks well and can serve as a drop-in replacement for Mechanical Turk, is unaffected, as is its one negative result on the healthcare rumor corrections.

Every number in a corrected sentence below is computed from the deposited replication archive ([10.7910/DVN/DDWWJW](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/DDWWJW)) at the time this document is rendered, including the numbers that were not wrong. Bold marks the corrections. The code and output supporting each correction are at [github.com/active-maintenance-aec/coppock_mcclellan_2019](https://github.com/active-maintenance-aec/coppock_mcclellan_2019). Entries 8 and 9 are the exception to all three: neither states a number, the evidence for both is the published PDF rather than the archive, and both were found by setting this edition's pages beside the published ones rather than by running anything.

The first two entries share a cause, and the seventh is why they no longer rest on it. Section 1 of the online appendix states that "we obtain two-tailed p-values under a normal approximation," and the deposited `12_DistanceTests.R` instead computes `pnorm(2 * (1 - abs(z)))`, which is not a p-value for any hypothesis. The two expressions differ in where they put the threshold: the deposit's calls a difference significant at the 0.05 level once `|z|` exceeds 1.82, where the two-tailed test needs 1.96. Read off the standard errors appendix Table 1 prints, extraversion is the only one of the 21 characteristics whose verdict falls between them, and the corrections below are what follows for the two sentences that count significant differences. Those printed standard errors are themselves a single draw from an unseeded bootstrap, which is entry 7. Under the seeded `r n_fmt(counts$n_resamples)`-resample bootstrap this note now runs, extraversion clears neither threshold, so both corrections hold whichever expression is used, and both are also recomputed from the distance and the standard error the published table prints, which do not move.

```{r rendered-entries, results="asis"}
walk(entries$entry, emit)
```

```{r emit-spine}
# The machine-readable spine, written wherever this document is rendered. Anything else
# that needs these entries reads it rather than keeping its own copy, so the two cannot
# drift.
# The spine's vocabularies are closed (cleanup of 2026-11-07): a value outside them is a
# typo, and the edition builders read these columns to shape every entry.
stopifnot(
  all(entries$class %in% c("quantity", "description", "interpretation", "definition", "label", "float", "cross_reference", "wording", "spelling", "typography", "bibliographic")),
  all(entries$form %in% c("full", "brief", "note")),
  all(entries$source %in% c("pipeline", "reading", "reference_audit", "publisher_record", "authors_archive", "proof"))
)
write_csv(select(entries, -any_of("values_in_spans")), here("errata_entries.csv"))
```
